To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ACOT approach can provide a consistent perturbatively based calculation of the inclusive and differential structure functions in deep inelastic charm production from threshold to high energy scales, and that the order αs 4-flavor calculations are accurate and reliable over a wide range of Q2.

(a) The 3-flavor and 4-flavor calculations of the inclusive cross section in deep inelastic lepton-nucleon scattering are consistent with each other, and with the experimental data, at least to order αs, and (b) The Monte Carlo implementation of the ACOT approach allows a systematic study of the differential distributions in a consistent PQCD framework.

(1) The 3- and 4-flavor MSbar schemes are smoothly connected in the generalized Collins formalism, and the 4-flavors scheme provides a good description of the inclusive structure functions in deep inelastic charm production at HERA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a consistent perturbatively-based approach to charm production in DIS.

the study of QCD processes in which the mass of a heavy quark plays a crucial role, such as the Drell-Yan process, the associated production of a heavy quarks and a gauge boson, and the production of heavy quark jets.
the development of the theoretical tools necessary for the extraction of information on the gluon structure of a nucleon from charm final states.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the 4-flavour scheme is a good approximation to the full 5-flavour scheme for the inclusive cross-sections, but that it is necessary to go to higher orders in αs to achieve the same level of accuracy in the case of the differential distributions.
the charm structure function is now well understood, at least at the level of the NLO approximation.

the ACOT approach provides a consistent framework for describing the charm production data at all Q2 and x, and that the order αs calculation is adequate for the inclusive cross-section but not for differential distributions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the charm structure functions are well described by a consistent order-αs calculation in the 4-flavour scheme, and that the transition from the 4-flavors to the 3-flavors is rather smooth and can be made to work well in the entire kinematic range.
the ACOT scheme provides a consistent perturbatively valid description of the inclusive cross section over the entire energy regime, from threshold to the asymptotic limit.
the 4-flavour scheme with a consistent resummation of large ln (mc2/Q 2) contributions provides a consistent framework for describing inclusive DIS cross-sections over a large kinematic range.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the charm contribution to inclusive F2 can be calculated with a precision comparable to the NLO 3-flavor calculation over the full measured energy range, provided the 3- to 4-flavor transition is carried out in a smooth manner.

the 4-flavors (mc≠0, αs=αs4) scheme is an excellent approximation to the full theory over a wide kinematic range, and is a viable alternative to the FFN (mc=0, αs4) scheme for phenomenological applications.
the ACOT approach provides a consistent framework for the interpretation of the inclusive HERA cross-section data over the full Q2 range, from threshold to high energy.
